segments.text: Good evening. You're tuned to First 100 Users: the things you saved about finding your first customers.
First, an essay you kept on September twenty-third.
You can't wait for users to come to you. You have to go out and get them.
Paul Graham. Same essay, on how the Collison brothers signed up Stripe's first users.
Right then, give me your laptop.
And from the Superhuman story you saved that same afternoon, one question.
How would you feel if you could no longer use the product?

source.title: How Superhuman Built an Engine to Find Product Market Fit

segments.text: Three founders. One move. Nobody waited to be found.
Between First 100 Users and Product Stories, Ancher found something both shelves agree on.
You win people not by selling your big vision, but by the benefit one real person feels right now.
You should take extraordinary measures not just to acquire users, but also to make them happy.
When you frame ninety percent around how your recipient benefits, they are much more likely to take action.

source.title: The Anatomy of a Great Cold Sales Pitch

segments.text: And the newest thing on your shelf, saved yesterday.
Most planning tools start from the entire internet and work down. This one starts from the handful of things someone already decided were worth keeping.
